text: PsiQuantum's fusion-based architecture handles photon loss as an erasure error. Why is that choice strategically important?
choices: Erasure errors require no error correction at all
Erasure lets the machine run at room temperature without single-photon detectors
Erasure errors enjoy a much higher correction threshold (of order 10% per photon) than general gate errors (about 1%)
Erasure converts the machine from a discrete-variable to a continuous-variable encoding
explanation: In fusion-based quantum computation the dominant error is photon loss, and treating it as a heralded erasure gives correction thresholds of order 10% per photon versus roughly 1% for general gate errors, a far more forgiving budget. Erasure still requires correction (not option 0), does not remove the need for cryogenic SNSPDs, and does not change the discrete-variable encoding.
